title: Marketplace listing screenshot + diagram plan (AWS + GCP) and capture/edit workflow
creator: Tessa Morgan
content:
## Context
We are refreshing AWS + GCP Marketplace listings. Partner review feedback + internal conversion analysis indicate our current visuals are outdated (old console IA, no clear Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private differentiation, no onboarding clarity).

This ticket defines:
1) The full visual asset inventory (screenshots + diagrams) required for AWS + GCP listing submissions.
2) Capture workflow (staging env, seeded data, redaction rules, review gates).
3) Format + localization constraints (so assets are reusable across AWS/GCP and don’t break if UI labels change).

Primary goals:
- Communicate product differentiation (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private/VPC/on‑prem)
- Show operational credibility (latency/cost observability, rollouts, audit logs)
- Reduce procurement/onboarding uncertainty (subscription → entitlement → org provisioning → first key)

Owners / reviewers:
- DRI (visual production): Alicia Perez
- Design review: Tessa Morgan
- PMM copy alignment: Soojin Lee
- Console correctness: Chloe Martin
- Security review (no sensitive data in screenshots): Marcus Lin / Naomi Feldman

---

## Asset inventory (v1) — what we will submit

### A) Hero + differentiation (used on both AWS + GCP)
1. **Hero: Redwood Console overview** (dashboard landing)
   - Purpose: “production inference platform” not “single model endpoint”
   - Shows: high-level usage/latency/cost tiles + model routing summary

2. **Deployment modes comparison visual (diagram)**
   - 1 panel with three columns: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private
   - Callouts: time-to-value, isolation, networking, SLAs, support

3. **Model catalog + pinned versions (screenshot)**
   - Shows: curated models, version pinning, rollout readiness
   - Avoid naming competitors; keep “Redwood-verified profiles” language

### B) Proof of production ops (Console)
4. **Latency & throughput chart with percentiles (screenshot)**
   - Shows p50/p95 + token/sec
   - Time range: last 24h

5. **Token-level cost breakdown (screenshot)**
   - Shows cost per route/model + caching/batching impact
   - MUST avoid exposing real customer names/ids

6. **Rollouts screen: canary / A/B + fallback policy (screenshot)**
   - Shows: two model versions, traffic split, “automatic fallback” toggle

7. **Error analysis / request traces (screenshot)**
   - Shows: one example trace with redacted prompt/response
   - Emphasize: “operational tooling” not “debugging user content”

### C) Marketplace onboarding (reduce time-to-first-success)
8. **Onboarding flow diagram (diagram)**
   - Subscription → Entitlement → Sign in / Create org → Link org → Create API key → First call → Metering
   - Includes “entitlement propagation delay” box + retry guidance

9. **Console onboarding: marketplace entrypoint (screenshot)**
   - Shows: provider selection (AWS/GCP) + entitlement check state

10. **Entitlement error state (screenshot)**
   - Shows: common failure (“entitlement not found yet”) + retry + support link
   - Must not mention internal systems; keep wording customer-friendly

11. **Success state: API key created + quickstart snippet (screenshot)**
   - Shows: copyable curl + streaming example toggle

### D) Security/compliance confidence (visual-only, not evidence)
12. **Security overview diagram (diagram)**
   - Data flow: customer app → Redwood API → inference runtime → logs/metrics
   - Callouts: encryption in transit/at rest, KMS options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), audit logs, retention controls
   - Avoid stating certifications in-image; point to docs in listing text

13. **Audit log viewer (screenshot)**
   - Shows: key events (API key created, role updated, org linked, export initiated)
   - All actor emails replaced with example domains (e.g., user@acme.example)


### Minimum set by marketplace (submission-safe)
- AWS: Items 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 11 (plus optional 6/12 if file count allows)
- GCP: Items 1, 2, 4, 8, 11 (keep security diagram optional depending on final listing constraints)

---

## Capture plan (where/how we’ll get screenshots)

### Environments
- Use **staging console** with production-like branding.
- Create seeded org: **“Acme Robotics (Staging)”** with demo projects/routes.
- Use demo users:
  - admin@acme.example
  - se@acme.example

### Data seeding rules
- Prompts/responses:
  - Use synthetic, non-sensitive text (no customer data, no real logs).
  - For trace view, show redacted/placeholder payloads.
- Usage charts:
  - Seed stable token/latency timeseries to avoid jagged visuals.

### Redaction rules (non-negotiable)
- Blur/remove:
  - API keys, tokens, request IDs, org IDs, billing account IDs, webhook secrets
  - Any “real” email domains (use .example)
- Avoid showing:
  - Internal feature flags
  - Debug headers
  - Raw prompts/responses beyond a short sanitized snippet

### Capture workflow
1) Alicia captures raw screenshots at 2x scale (Retina)
2) Drop into Figma frame templates (see “Marketplace Listing Assets” file)
3) Apply redaction + consistency edits (font smoothing, alignment)
4) Export to PNG (primary) + optional JPG (secondary if file size issues)
5) Review gates:
   - Design (Tessa): visual clarity + narrative coherence
   - PMM (Soojin): copy alignment + prohibited claims check
   - Security (Marcus/Naomi): no sensitive data, compliant wording
   - Console owner (Chloe): UI accuracy vs release branch

---

## Format constraints + guidelines

### General
- **Aspect ratio:** Prefer 16:9 frames; avoid ultra-wide crops.
- **Resolution:** Provide master exports at 3840×2160 (or equivalent 2x) and downscale as needed.
- **File size:** Target <2MB per image (optimize with TinyPNG after approvals).
- **Background:** Keep consistent (light theme) unless dark theme improves contrast; do not mix themes in a single set.
- **Text density:** Keep readable on marketplace pages; avoid tiny text. Use zoomed crops over full-page shots.

### AWS Marketplace-specific (practical)
- Avoid images that look like ads; keep product-forward.
- Don’t include pricing, discount language, or “best/fastest” superlatives in the image itself.

### GCP Marketplace-specific (practical)
- Favor fewer, higher-signal screenshots. Ensure the first two images explain “what it is” and “how it works”.

### Localization / future-proofing
- Default: **English-only** assets for launch.
- Keep assets localization-friendly:
  - Avoid embedding long sentences in images.
  - Prefer callouts with 1–3 word labels (e.g., “Fallback policy”, “Audit logs”).
  - Avoid region-specific currency or date formats.
  - Avoid hard-coding provider names inside console UI shots when possible (use “Marketplace” generic label).

---

## Deliverables
- Figma: “Marketplace Listing Assets (AWS+GCP) – 2026 Refresh”
  - Page: Screenshot frames (16:9 templates)
  - Page: Diagram components + export variants
- Export package:
  - /exports/aws/ (PNG)
  - /exports/gcp/ (PNG)
  - /exports/source/ (Figma links + notes)

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Asset inventory approved by PMM + Partnerships (AWS/GCP)
- [x] Capture workflow documented with redaction rules
- [x] Figma templates created and shared
- [x] Final exports produced and linked in the listing asset checklist
- [x] Security review sign-off recorded before partner submission

---

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Do we need separate assets per provider?
  - A: No; keep a unified set and only swap the onboarding entrypoint screenshot if provider-specific UI is unavoidable.
- Q: Can we show SOC 2/ISO badges in images?
  - A: No. Keep certifications in text/docs only to avoid outdated claims in static images.

---
